question: Political pluralism in the media is a fundamental principle enshrined in Article 11 of the EU Charter of Fundamental Rights. It is also a central objective of the European Democracy Shield presented by the Commission, which aims to strengthen the EU’s democratic resilience by ensuring a pluralistic, balanced and independent media environment.

The Media Freedom Act, which entered into application in the summer of 2025, follows that rationale by requiring public media to be strictly politically neutral and to ensure fair representation of different democratic preferences.

However, a study carried out by the Institut Thomas More for Le Figaro Magazine and published in November 20251 reveals a worrying imbalance: Radio France’s editorial line reportedly systematically favours left-leaning personalities and discourse, while adopting an openly hostile stance towards certain opposition parties, not least the Rassemblement National, which is portrayed as an agent of political disorder. 1.
Is the Commission aware of any evaluations demonstrating a lack of pluralism within Radio France or French public broadcasting, or of any reports that such is the case?

How does it intend to ensure that the objectives of the European Democracy Shield, including the promotion of a truly pluralistic media environment, are respected by the public media in the Member States?
Supporters2
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (20.2.2026) The EU’s commitment to respect media freedom and pluralism and to uphold freedom of expression is enshrined in the Charter of Fundamental Rights of the European Union. These core values of the EU, underpin a number of EU initiatives, including the European Media Freedom Act (EMFA)1, in application since 8 August 2025.

The EMFA establishes a common framework to safeguard editorial independence, pluralism and the autonomy of public service media. Article 5 EMFA requires Member States to ensure that public service media operate independently and are protected from political interference.

They have to designate independent authorities or bodies or put in place mechanisms free from political influence, to monitor the application of this provision. The Commission is in close contact with all Member States to ensure the alignment of their legal frameworks with the EMFA.

More broadly, the objectives of the European Democracy Shield will continue to be pursued through a combination of legislative measures, policy initiatives and support for independent journalism and media literacy, including funding tools. The Commission is not aware of any official assessment establishing a lack of political pluralism within Radio France or French public service broadcasting more generally.
The Commission will continue to monitor media freedom and pluralism in the Member States through the annual Rule of Law Report and relevant EU legislation.
1 Regulation (EU) 2024/1083 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 11 April 2024 establishing a
common framework for media services in the internal market and amending Directive 2010/13/EU (European Media Freedom Act) (Text with EEA relevance).
